## 보관 원문

> # Kim et al. 2026 — Fe production from ores by 1,173 K molten oxide electrolysis
>
> - Title: Production of Fe metal from Fe ores through novel molten oxide electrolysis at 1173 K
> - Journal: Scientific Reports
> - DOI: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-026-58521-y
> - PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42414383/
> - Authors: Joongseok Kim; Jungshin Kang; Kyung-Woo Yi
> - Published online: 2026-07-07
> - Collected: 2026-07-28
> - Funding disclosed: Korea Institute of Energy Technology Evaluation and Planning; POSCO
> - Peer review: journal research article
>
> ## Experimental scope
>
> - The authors investigated iron oxides and three iron ores in a
>   B2O3–Na2O molten oxide at 1,173 K.
> - Electrolysis was conducted at 1.6 V in air or argon. Reported current
>   efficiencies for reagent iron oxides were 65.50–68.72% in air and
>   67.49–78.56% in argon, with the increase attributed to suppression of
>   re-oxidation at low oxygen partial pressure.
> - Hematite, goethite and magnetite ores electrolyzed in air yielded reported
>   current efficiencies of 64.14%, 66.00% and 67.58%, respectively.
> - Metallic iron formed on a platinum cathode as a Pt–Fe solid-solution alloy
>   with dendritic particles nearby; the tested impurity oxides were not reduced
>   at the applied voltage.
>
> ## Technology boundary
>
> - This is a laboratory feasibility result for a borate-based molten oxide at
>   1,173 K and a platinum cathode. It does not establish an industrially durable
>   cathode or anode, continuous tapping, energy consumption, electrolyte life,
>   refractory life, ore-feed rate, product-separation method or commercial
>   economics.
> - The route is materially different from Boston Metal's roughly 1,600°C MOE
>   Steel configuration that targets liquid iron collected at the cell bottom.
>   Both are molten-oxide electrolysis, but their temperature, product state,
>   electrolyte and scale-up problems must not be merged.
> - POSCO funding establishes a research connection, not deployment of this cell
>   design in HyREX or another POSCO commercial project.
